claim: Experts describe troubleshooting complexity as four kinds (system representation, information ambiguity, situational, stakeholder) and five misaligned layers; this comes from one interview study of 18 senior engineers with no statistics.
agent_test: Add a complexity-type triage at S0 (which of the four kinds dominates) and compare to no triage at equal tokens on AIOpsLab/SREGym problems.

claim: Expert troubleshooting is non-linear and recursive: experts revisit system understanding, root-cause search and evidence checks, rather than following a fixed sequence.
agent_test: Allow a back-edge from any state to system modelling; compare with a one-way pipeline at equal tokens.

claim: Experts build a model of normal operation or design intent before diagnosing (concept of operations, flow charts, customer account of what happened just before failure).
agent_test: Force a short normal-behaviour model step before hypotheses; measure RCA accuracy on SREGym/AIOpsLab.

claim: Explicit modelling, prediction, comparison and then proposal is the observed loop in student troubleshooting; split-half testing is the common strategy; partner negotiation about when to move on sits outside the model.
agent_test: Require a stated prediction before each tool call and a comparison after; count wasted calls.

claim: Structured Troubleshooting (domain-independent strategy plus functional decomposition) doubled the number of malfunctions solved in a technician study; read from abstract only. Gap search: still abstract only; no N, times or replication found.
agent_test: Add multi-level functional decomposition (system, subsystem, device, component) before hypothesis generation.

claim: LLM agent accuracy falls as the task moves from detection to localisation to root cause to mitigation (AIOpsLab: detection 23-100%, RCA 9-45%, mitigation 0-36%).
agent_test: Report per-stage accuracy; test whether a verify step raises RCA at equal tokens.

claim: Frontier agents solve few real SRE incidents and success drops with scenario difficulty (ITBench 13.8% SRE; GPT-4o diagnosis 36/7.7/5.0% easy/medium/hard); new harder failure types drop end-to-end success from about 60% to 15-28% (SREGym).
agent_test: Evaluate on hard split only; difficulty-stratified reporting.

claim: Diagnosis and repair are decoupled for LLM agents: agents sometimes mitigate with a wrong cause belief and sometimes diagnose right but cannot repair; run-to-run variance is large.
agent_test: Check whether a mitigation is consistent with the stated cause before submitting; use repeated runs.

claim: Diagnosis quality is the repair bottleneck: human-written bug explanations lift GPT-4 repair from 33.3% to 52.6%; self-repair at equal compute is about equal to resampling (1.05x and 0.97x).
agent_test: Compare diagnose-then-repair against plain resampling at equal tokens.

claim: Self-correction without an external signal does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0), and no prompted-LLM feedback success is known in general tasks; reliable external feedback (tools, oracle) is what works.
agent_test: Ground every revision in a tool output or test result; ban pure re-reading revisions.

claim: Early commitment and anchoring damage agents: multi-turn underspecified input drops performance by 39%; off-the-shelf o3 anchors on first impressions; RCA agents accept the first anomaly as root cause (symptom-as-cause) and explore incompletely.
agent_test: Add a mandatory second hypothesis and a disconfirming test before commit; measure symptom-as-cause rate.

claim: Structured multi-role orchestration with hypothesis tracking and a challenger role raised sequential-diagnosis accuracy (o3 78.6% to 81.9% at lower cost; 85.5% with ensembling) while physicians reached 20%. Gap search: the paper has no single-role ablation, so the effect of the challenger or hypothesis tracker alone is not isolated.
agent_test: Port hypothesis table plus challenger turn into scaffold; compare to plain model at equal tokens.

claim: Choosing questions by expected information gain raises success in diagnosis and troubleshooting dialogues (FloDial GPT-4 43.7 to 67.3 absolute points; average +38.1% over direct prompting).
agent_test: Rank candidate tests by expected hypothesis-set reduction; compare with arbitrary order.

claim: Prompt-level fixes do not remove RCA failures: hypothesis-driven and pitfall-aware prompts left perfect-answer rates near 0 to 7%, and hallucinated reading of data persisted.
agent_test: Test whether an enforced quote-the-data step (not a prompt warning) cuts hallucinated readings.

claim: Encoding expert procedures (SOPs) as retrievable knowledge and executable steps beats ReAct, Reflexion and CoT for RCA (average accuracy 64.01 vs ReAct 35.50), and retrieved similar past incidents also help. Flow-of-Action ablation (GPT-3.5, 90 incidents, one system): removing SOP knowledge dropped average accuracy 54.06 to 15.39; no unseen-fault-family test.
agent_test: Store solved-fault records and retrieve similar ones at S0; measure on repeated fault families.

claim: Context management and trajectory self-consistency materially stabilise tool-using RCA agents (RCAgent pass rate 99.38% full; large drops when components removed).
agent_test: Ablate context compaction on long troubleshooting runs.

claim: Ticket or symptom framing changes agent outcome: a vague report cut Claude Code from .870 to .283 on healthy networks and over-diagnosis rose from 17% to 47%; confident wrong tickets are handled like accurate ones because they can be tested.
agent_test: Add an early step: is a fault present at all, and what would refute the report. Test on false-premise tasks.

claim: Agents do not know when to stop on healthy systems: they over-diagnose false reports and burn budget on timeouts (9% of runs used 23% of spend).
agent_test: Add a no-fault exit criterion and a step cap; measure false-alarm rate and tokens.

claim: More steps help only to a point: environment-feedback agents plateau after about 5 steps in AIOpsLab while tokens grow; NIKA shows token use nearly doubling at larger topology without matching accuracy.
agent_test: Plot accuracy against step budget for scaffold and plain at equal tokens.

claim: Fault-diagnosis accuracy falls with network or system size and multi-evidence demands: localisation and RCA drop with topology size while detection stays stable; 62.5% of cases need 2 or more data types.
agent_test: Test a cross-source evidence fusion step on multi-source cases.

claim: Human discussion text added to incident input did not significantly improve root-cause predictions, while fine-tuned models do slightly better on machine-detected incidents.
agent_test: Low priority; test whether extra unstructured context helps with and without a filtering step.

claim: Debugging difficulty rises with number and type of simultaneous bugs, and low-level runtime feedback does not help logic bugs (GPT-4: 93.6% missing colon, 55.9% quadruple bugs).
agent_test: Isolate one fault at a time before fixing; compare with fixing all at once.

claim: Agent-system traces are hard to diagnose zero-shot: fault-type top-1 at most about 25% for the best model, with a no-fault reference trace helping somewhat.
agent_test: Provide a known-good reference run at S0 for comparisons.

claim: Interview-based expert studies are small and preliminary; sample numbers differ between sources (18 vs 22 interviews) and no outcome test of the proposed scaffolds exists.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; a warning on how much weight the human evidence can bear.

claim: No published ablation separates the roles inside MAI-DxO (hypothesis tracker, test chooser, challenger, stewardship, checklist). Only variants (budget, ensemble, question-only) and single versus batched mode were reported; single mode matched batched accuracy (83.9%) at lower cost ($3,991 vs $5,084).
agent_test: Run our own role-by-role ablation at equal cost on a diagnosis set.

claim: Ensembling several independent diagnostic panels with an aggregation step gave the highest accuracy in MAI-DxO (85.5% vs 81.9% single panel) at the cost of plain o3, so part of the headline gain may come from sampling and aggregation, not role-play.
agent_test: Compare single panel, k independent samples with vote, and role panel at equal tokens.

claim: LLM help for physical hardware (analog circuit) debugging has only qualitative evidence: 17 student chat logs and one student case; LLMs often named the true root cause but misread wiring photos and stated high confidence while wrong. No measured non-IT fault benchmark was found.
agent_test: Tie any stated confidence to evidence the agent has actually observed; treat photo-based readings as unverified.

claim: Triage by complexity type at S0, a no-fault gate, and enforced quote-before-interpret grounding have no tested effect in the literature found; they remain untested proposals.
agent_test: Ablate each at equal tokens on SREGym or AIOpsLab.

claim: Outcome-only RCA scoring can reward keyword luck; a reasoning-process benchmark (AIOps2025, RCA100) scores evidence checkpoints and uses deterministic matching, but no published human re-score of agent grading was found.
agent_test: Score our agent's trace for quoted evidence as well as the final label.
